title: Tale of the Singer and the Druggist (मराठी)

keywords: tale of the singer and the druggist
full_text:
In a quiet quarter of Cairo lived an impoverished young musician named Tariq, whose voice upon the lute was sweet as running water, and an honest herbal druggist named Abu Ahmad, whose shop was filled with fragrant jars of camphor, myrrh, and dried chamomile.

Whenever Tariq was penniless, the kind druggist fed him warm bread and lentils, never demanding payment, saying: 'Sing me a verse of your homeland, brother; your melody is a medicine for my soul richer than all the balsams of Arabia.'

One winter, a royal courier from Baghdad arrived in Cairo, seeking the finest musician in Egypt for the court of the Caliph. Tariq was chosen, taken to the Abbasid palace, and rewarded with robes of honor and three thousand gold dinars.

Instead of forgetting his humble beginnings, Tariq’s first thought was of the honest druggist who had shared his bread.

He returned to Cairo with four mules laden with silks, porcelain, and two thousand gold dinars, presenting them to Abu Ahmad before all the merchants of the bazaar:

'Ten years ago, you gave me medicine for my body and belief in my art; today, I return to repay your bread with gold!'

Abu Ahmad embraced the young master with tears of joy. Together, they established a free clinic and music conservatory for the poor youth of Cairo, proving that true friendship and gratitude are the highest virtues of civilization.
moral: Kindness and mutual support between humble artisans create a bond that outlasts fortune. [MR]
